name: The Victory of the Lamb and the Defeat of Evil
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ

objectives.text: Identify Jesus as the Lamb who wins the victory over evil in Revelation
Name Jesus as the rider on the white horse who is called Faithful and True and King of kings and Lord of lords
Retell how God's people in heaven sing praise because the Lamb has won the victory
Recall that God will one day throw Satan away forever so that he can never harm God's people again
Explain that Jesus won his victory over sin and Satan by dying on the cross and rising again, as shown by the Lamb who was slain
Summarize the Marriage Supper of the Lamb and what it shows about Christ's love for his church
Explain from Scripture that death itself will be defeated and thrown into the lake of fire
Describe how the followers of the Lamb overcome the dragon by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony
Compare the temporary and limited power of evil with the eternal reign of God as Revelation presents them
Identify the main events of Christ's final defeat of the beast, the false prophet, and Satan in Revelation 19 and 20
Explain the Reformed teaching that Christ as King restrains and conquers all his and his people's enemies
Describe the amillennial, postmillennial, and premillennial views and the reading of Revelation 20:1-6 that each one holds
Analyze the binding of Satan in Revelation 20:1-3 by connecting it to Jesus' teaching on binding the strong man and casting out the ruler of this world
Explain how the Great White Throne judgment displays God's justice through judgment according to works and the Book of Life
Explain the meaning of the second death and contrast it with the first resurrection
Explain from Scripture why believers are openly acknowledged and acquitted in the day of judgment through Christ
Compare the main millennial views by constructing a timeline of the last things for each and evaluating how each handles the text of Revelation 19 and 20
Explain the Reformed teaching that the day of judgment is certain while its hour is unknown and why Scripture therefore calls believers to watchfulness
Analyze how Revelation's message of the Lamb's victory answers the cry of persecuted believers for justice
Defend from Scripture the bodily and visible return of Christ as the church has confessed it
Evaluate how God's final judgment vindicates his holiness and displays both his mercy and his justice
Construct a biblically supported account of Christ's victory that traces it from the cross to the final defeat of every enemy

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (Lamb's victory, white horse rider, Satan's final defeat, heavenly celebration, Marriage Supper, death's defeat, temporary vs eternal power, binding of Satan, Great White Throne, second death, millennial timeline, persecuted believers, Christ's bodily return, vindication of God's holiness). Replaced vague items such as 'Identify the final judgment' and 'Analyze the Millennium' with concrete tasks: identifying the sequence of the beast's, false prophet's, and Satan's defeat, describing the three millennial views, and later comparing them. Recast 'Evaluate the comfort' as an analysis of the text so that no objective targets feeling. Added missing competencies: victory won through the cross, overcoming by the blood of the Lamb, Christ's kingly office (WSC Q26), believers' acquittal at judgment (WSC Q38), the certainty and unknown hour of the day (WCF 33.3), and a capstone synthesis. Replaced the single confession citation with specific articles from the WCF, WSC, Heidelberg, and Belgic. Left the New Jerusalem and symbolism material to the sibling sub-topics.
